en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Visualization of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, translated by the Tripitaka Master Kang-lang-ye-she of the Western Regions during the Song Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
and thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas, with the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī as their leader.

At that time, in the great city of Rājagṛha, there was a crown prince named Ajātaśatru. Following the instructions of his evil friend Devadatta, he arrested his father, King Bimbisāra, and confined him within seven layers of chambers, forbidding all the ministers from approaching him under any circumstances.

The Queen Mother of the state, named Vaidehī, paid respectful homage to the Great King; having bathed herself until she was pure, she mixed parched grain with ghee and honey and anointed her body with it. She placed grape juice within various necklaces and secretly offered them to the King.
At that time, the Great King, having eaten parched grain and drunk gruel, sought water to rinse his mouth;
having finished rinsing his mouth, he joined his palms in reverence, bowed from afar toward Vulture Peak to the World-Honored One, and spoke these words:
"Mahāmaudgalyāyana is my close friend; I pray that you will arouse compassion and grant me the eight precepts."
At that time, Maudgalyāyana flew like a hawk or a falcon and arrived swiftly at the king’s location;
he did so every day in this manner, bestowing upon the king the eight precepts.
The World-Honored One also dispatched the Venerable Pūrṇa to preach the Dharma for the king.
After this period of twenty-one days had passed, because King [Ajātaśatru] had eaten parched grain with honey and heard the Dharma, his complexion became harmonious and joyful.
At that time, Ajātaśatru asked the gatekeeper:
"Does my father, the King, still live?"
Then the gatekeeper addressed him, saying:
"Great King! The Queen Mother of the State has smeared her body with parched grain and honey, and wearing ornaments filled with wine, she brings them to offer to Your Majesty."
"The śramaṇa Maudgalyāyana and Pūrṇa have come through the air to preach the Dharma to the king; they cannot be restrained.
When Ajātaśatru heard these words, he said angrily to his mother, "My mother is a thief, and she has become an accomplice to thieves!"
"This wicked śramaṇa uses illusory deceptions and incantations to cause this evil king not to die for many days.
He then seized a sharp sword, intending to kill his mother.
At that time, there was a minister named Candraprabha (Moonlight), who was intelligent and possessed great wisdom; together with Jīvaka, he paid homage to the king.
He addressed him, saying: "Great King!
Your servant has heard it stated in the Vedas:..."
"Since the beginning of the kalpa, there have been wicked kings who, out of greed for the throne, have murdered their fathers eighteen thousand times;
yet I have never heard of one who, lacking the Way, harmed his mother."
"Your Majesty has now committed this act of parricide, defiling the Kṣatriya lineage; we cannot bear to hear of it!
You are a Caṇḍāla; it is no longer fitting for us to remain here."
When the two ministers had finished speaking these words, they gripped their swords with their hands and withdrew,
retreating backward. At that moment, Ajātaśatru was struck with alarm and dread, and he said to Jīvaka,
"Will you not act for my sake?"
Jīva addressed him, saying:
"Great King! Be careful not to harm your mother."
Upon hearing these words, the king repented and sought deliverance; he immediately cast away his sword and desisted from harming his mother, then commanded his inner officials:
"Shut him up in the deep palace and do not allow him to come out again."
At that time, having been confined in seclusion, Vaidehī was distressed and emaciated with grief.
She turned toward Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, paid homage to the Buddha, and spoke these words:
"In the past, when the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, was still in the world, he constantly sent Ānanda to come and comfort me."
"I am now filled with sorrow and anxiety; because the World-Honored One is so majestic and grave, there is no way for me to see him.
I pray that you will dispatch Maudgalyāyana or the Venerable Ānanda to meet with me."
Having spoken these words, she wept with tears falling like rain and prostrated herself toward the Buddha from afar.

Before her head had even been raised, the World-Honored One, who was on Vulture Peak Mountain, knew the thoughts in Vaidehī’s mind and immediately commanded Mahāmaudgalyāyana and Ānanda to come through the air.
The Buddha vanished from Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa and appeared in the royal palace.
At that time, Vaidehī, having prostrated, raised her head and beheld the World-Honored One, Śākyamuni Buddha, his body the color of purple-gold, seated upon a lotus flower made of a hundred jewels.
Maudgalyāyana attended on his left and Ānanda was on his right; Śakra, Brahmā, and the world-protecting devas were in the void, raining down celestial flowers everywhere as an offering.
At that time, when Vaidehī beheld the Buddha, the World-Honored One, she tore off her own jeweled necklace, threw herself prostrate upon the ground,
and wailed toward the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One!..."
"What sins did I commit in my past lives that I have given birth to such a wicked son?
Furthermore, by what causes and conditions has the World-Honored One formed a kinsmanly bond with Devadatta?

I only pray that the World-Honored One will extensively explain for me the realm free from sorrow and affliction, where I shall be reborn; I take no pleasure in this turbid and evil world of Jambudvīpa."
In this turbid and evil place, hells, hungry ghosts, and animals abound, and there is a great accumulation of unwholesome things.
May I, in the future, never hear evil sounds nor see evil people.
"Now, prostrating myself before the World-Honored One with my five limbs touching the ground, I seek your compassion and repent.
I only pray that the Buddha-Sun will instruct me in the contemplation of the sphere of pure karma.
At that time, the World-Honored One emitted light from between his eyebrows; the light was golden in color and shone everywhere throughout the immeasurable worlds of the ten directions.
It returned to rest atop the Buddha’s crown and transformed into a golden terrace as vast as Mount Sumeru.
Within it, the pure and wondrous lands of the Buddhas of the ten directions all appeared.
Some of these lands were composed of the seven treasures;
Furthermore, there are lands that consist entirely of lotus flowers;
furthermore, there are lands like the palaces of the Lord of Sovereignty (Īśvara);
furthermore, there are lands like crystal mirrors.
The lands of the ten directions all appear therein.
Such immeasurable Buddha-lands, magnificent and beautiful to behold, were made visible to Vaidehī.
At that time, Vaidehī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Although these buddha-lands are pure and all possess radiance;”
"I now desire to be born in the world of Ultimate Bliss, in the presence of Amitābha Buddha.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will instruct me in contemplation and instruct me in right concentration.
At that time, the World-Honored One smiled, and five-colored rays of light issued from his mouth; each ray of light shone upon the crown of King Bimbisāra’s head.

At that time, although the Great King was confined in seclusion, his mental eye was unobstructed; seeing the World-Honored One from afar, he prostrated himself in homage and spontaneously advanced to attain the stage of Anāgāmin.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Vaidehī:
"Do you know now? Amitābha Buddha is not far from here."
"You should fix your mindfulness and contemplate with clarity those who have accomplished pure karma in that land.
I shall now explain many parables for you, so that all ordinary persons of future ages who wish to cultivate pure karma may attain birth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss."
Those who wish to be born in that land should cultivate three kinds of merit:
first, filially supporting one's parents, serving teachers and elders, maintaining a compassionate heart and refraining from killing, and practicing the ten virtuous actions.
Second, they receive and uphold the Three Refuges, fully observe the various precepts, and do not violate the rules of dignified conduct.
Third, they resolve to attain Bodhicitta, have deep faith in cause and effect, recite the Mahāyāna sūtras, and exhort practitioners to advance on the path.
"These three matters are called pure karma.
The Buddha said to Vaidehī:
"Do you understand now?"
"These three types of karma are the true causes for the pure karma of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
The Buddha told Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively!"
Reflect upon this well.
The Tathāgata now, for the sake of all sentient beings in future ages who are harmed by the thieves of affliction, shall proclaim the karma of purity.
Excellent, Vaidehī! You have asked this matter well. Ānanda!
"You should receive and uphold this, and extensively proclaim these words of the Buddha for the sake of the great multitude.
The Tathāgata now instructs Vaidehī and all sentient beings of future ages to contemplate the Western World of Ultimate Bliss."
By the power of the Buddha, they shall behold that pure land as clearly as seeing one's own facial reflection in a bright mirror.

Seeing the most wondrous and blissful matters of that land, their hearts will be filled with joy, and they shall immediately attain the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
The Buddha told Vaidehī: "You are an ordinary person;
your mental conceptions are weak and inferior, and as you have not yet attained the divine eye, you cannot see from afar.
The Tathāgatas possess extraordinary skillful means that will enable you to see."
At that time, Vaidehī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Just as I do now, by the power of the Buddha, I behold that land.”

If, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, all sentient beings are defiled, evil, and unwholesome, and are oppressed by the five sufferings, how shall they be able to see Amitābha Buddha and the world of Ultimate Bliss?
The Buddha told Vaidehī:
"You and all sentient beings should concentrate your minds and fix your thoughts on a single point, visualizing the western direction.
How should you form this visualization?"
Regarding all who practice visualization: among all sentient beings, unless one is born blind, those with eyes will all see the sun set.
You should form this mental image while sitting upright facing west; contemplate the sun intently, causing the mind to dwell firmly and remain focused without shifting.
Seeing the sun about to set, its shape resembling a suspended drum;
having seen the sun, one should ensure it is clearly perceived whether with eyes closed or open.
This is the visualization of the sun, called the first contemplation.
"One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation;
one who contemplates otherwise is said to practice wrong contemplation.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"Once the initial visualization is accomplished, next one should form the mental image of water.

One should visualize that everything in the western direction is entirely great water; seeing the water as clear and transparent, one should also maintain clarity of mind without any sense of distraction."
Having seen the water, one should form the perception of ice.
Seeing the ice as transparent and clear, one forms the perception of lapis lazuli.
Once this perception is established, one sees the ground of lapis lazuli, transparent both inside and out.
Below, there are golden vajra-staffs made of the seven treasures, supporting the lapis lazuli ground.

These staffs have eight sides with eight facets fully formed; each side is composed of a hundred jewels, and each jewel emits a thousand rays of light. Each ray of light possesses eighty-four thousand colors, which reflect upon the lapis lazuli ground like ten billion suns, such that they cannot be fully beheld.

Upon the ground of lapis lazuli, golden cords were interspersed and interwoven; demarcated by boundaries of the seven treasures, they were clearly defined, and within each treasure there were five hundred colored rays of light.
The light was like flowers and resembled the stars and moon; suspended in the void, it formed a radiant pavilion.
Within it were thousands of myriads of towers and galleries composed of a hundred jewels. On both sides of the pavilion were ten billion flower-banners, adorned with immeasurable musical instruments.

Eight kinds of pure breezes emerge from the radiance and strike these musical instruments, producing sounds that expound suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self; this is the perception of water, called the second visualization.
When this visualization is accomplished, observe each detail until it is perfectly clear.
Whether with eyes closed or open, do not allow the image to be lost; except for the time of eating, one should constantly keep this matter in mind.
"One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation;
one who contemplates otherwise is said to practice wrong contemplation.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"Once the perception of water has been accomplished, it is called a coarse vision of the land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
If one attains samādhi and sees that land, it will be perceived with such clarity and distinctness that it cannot be fully described."
"This is the perception of earth; it is called the third contemplation.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Retain these words of the Buddha and, for the sake of all the great assemblies in future ages who wish to be liberated from suffering, preach this method of contemplating the earth."
If one contemplates this ground, the offenses of birth and death accumulated over eighty billion kalpas will be eliminated.
After casting off this body in another world, one will certainly be reborn in a pure land; let the mind be free from doubt.
"One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation;
if one contemplates otherwise, it is called wrong contemplation.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"Once the perception of the ground has been established, one next contemplates the jewel trees.
As for contemplating the jewel trees, one contemplates each one individually, forming the perception of seven rows of trees.
Each tree is eight thousand yojanas high, and among all those jewel trees, there is none that is not fully endowed with flowers and leaves made of the seven treasures."
Each individual petal of the flower displays the color of a different jewel:
from within the lapis lazuli-colored petals, golden light radiates;
from within the crystal-colored petals, crimson light radiates.
From within the color of agate, the luster of musāragalva emerges;
from within the color of musāragalva, the luster of green pearls emerges;
and all manner of jewels, such as coral and amber, serve as radiant adornments.

Exquisite nets of true pearls completely covered the tops of the trees; upon each tree were seven layers of nets, and within each net-space were five hundred billion exquisite flower-palaces, like the palaces of the Brahma King.
The youths of the devas were spontaneously present therein; each youth wore a necklace made of five hundred billion *śakrābhilagna* mani jewels.

The light of these mani jewels illuminated a hundred *yojanas*, like the combined radiance of ten billion suns and moons, beyond all naming, with various jewels interspersed as the most excellent of colors.

These jewel trees stand in orderly rows, their leaves overlapping one another; from between the leaves grow various exquisite flowers, upon which there naturally appear fruits made of the seven treasures.
Each leaf of every tree was twenty-five yojanas in length and breadth, exactly equal;
the leaves possessed a thousand colors with a hundred kinds of patterns, like celestial garlands,
and bore many exquisite flowers of Jambūnada gold.
Like a whirling fire-wheel, it turns gracefully among the leaves, producing various fruits that emerge like the vase of Śakra;
it possesses great radiance, transforming into banners, streamers, and immeasurable jeweled canopies.
Within this jeweled canopy, all the Buddha-activities of the trichiliocosm are reflected;
the Buddha-lands of the ten directions likewise appear therein.
Having seen this tree, one should also successively contemplate it part by part, clearly visualizing the trunk, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits until they are all distinct.
This is the contemplation on the tree, called the fourth visualization.
One who practices this visualization is said to practice right observation;
one who observes otherwise is said to practice perverse observation.
The Buddha told Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"Once the visualization of the trees is accomplished, you should next visualize water.
To visualize the water: in the land of Sukhāvatī, there are eight pools of water."
Each pool of water is composed of the seven treasures;
these jewels are soft and supple, produced from the king of wish-fulfilling gems, and branch out into fourteen streams,
each stream manifesting the colors of the seven treasures.
The channels were made of gold, and their beds beneath were all composed of various colored diamonds as fine sand.
Within each stream were sixty billion lotus flowers made of the seven treasures; each lotus was perfectly round and measured twelve yojanas in diameter.
The streams of mani-jewels flow among the flowers, ascending and descending along the trees.

Their sound is subtle and exquisite, expounding upon suffering, emptiness, impermanence, non-self, and the various pāramitās; furthermore, there are those that praise the primary and secondary marks of the Buddhas.

From the king of wish-fulfilling jewels, subtle golden light emerges; this light transforms into birds of a hundred jewel-like colors, whose harmonious cries are plaintive and elegant, constantly praising mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, and mindfulness of the Sangha. This is the visualization of the water of eight virtues, called the fifth contemplation.
"One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation;
one who contemplates otherwise is said to practice wrong contemplation.
The Buddha then addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"In each of the worlds of these lands of manifold jewels, there are five hundred billion jeweled towers; within those pavilions dwell immeasurable devas, performing celestial music."
Furthermore, there were musical instruments suspended in mid-air, like celestial jeweled banners, which resounded spontaneously without being struck.
Amidst these various sounds, all proclaimed mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, and mindfulness of the Saṃgha of bhikṣus.

When this visualization is accomplished, it is called "roughly seeing" the jeweled trees, jeweled grounds, and jeweled ponds of the Land of Ultimate Bliss; this constitutes the general visualization and is known as the sixth contemplation.
If one sees this, the extremely heavy evil karma of immeasurable billions of kalpas will be eliminated, and after the end of life, one will certainly be born in that land.
One who performs this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation.
"If one views it otherwise, it is called false viewing.
The Buddha told Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively!"
Reflect upon this well.
I shall analyze and explain for you the Dharma for the removal of suffering and affliction; you should remember and uphold it, and analyze and explain it extensively for the great assembly.
When these words were spoken, Amitāyus Buddha stood poised in mid-air, with the two great beings Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta standing in attendance at his left and right.
The radiance was so blazing and intense that it could not be fully beheld; even the gold of a hundred thousand Jambūnada rivers could not be compared to it.
Having seen the Buddha Amitāyus, Vaidehī prostrated herself at his feet and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
By the power of the Buddha, I have now been able to see Amitāyus Buddha and the two Bodhisattvas; how, then, should future sentient beings visualize Amitāyus Buddha and the two Bodhisattvas?
The Buddha told Vaidehī:

"If you wish to behold that Buddha, you should give rise to mental visualization. On a ground of seven precious jewels, imagine a lotus flower, such that each petal of that lotus displays the colors of a hundred jewels."
There are eighty-four thousand channels, like celestial paintings;
within each channel there are eighty-four thousand rays of light, all clearly distinct and visible to everyone.
The smaller petals were two hundred and fifty yojanas in length and breadth;
thus, this lotus had eighty-four thousand great petals, and between each petal, there were ten billion mani-jewel kings serving as radiant ornaments.
Each mani-jewel emitted a thousand rays of light; these lights formed canopies composed of the seven treasures, covering the ground everywhere.
A śākkhara-vaiḍūrya-maṇi jewel served as the pedestal for these lotus thrones;
these lotus pedestals were further adorned with eighty thousand diamond *cintāmaṇi* jewels, brahma-maṇi jewels, and exquisite nets of pearls, interlaced and embellished.
Upon that terrace, four jeweled banners spontaneously appeared; each jeweled banner was like hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Mount Sumerus.
The jeweled canopies atop the banners were like those in the palaces of the Yāma Heaven, further adorned with five hundred billion exquisite precious jewels.

Each and every jewel bead emits eighty-four thousand rays of light; each ray produces eighty-four thousand different kinds of golden hues, and each golden hue pervades the entire jeweled land, manifesting various transformations in every place, each assuming a distinct appearance.

Some become diamond pedestals, some become nets of pearls, and some become clouds of variegated flowers; they manifest at will throughout the ten directions, performing the Buddha-work. This is the visualization of the flower seat, called the Seventh Meditation.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"These wondrous flowers were produced by the power of the vows of the bhikṣu Dharmākara. If you wish to bring that Buddha to mind, you should first form the mental image of this wondrous flower seat."
When forming this visualization, one must not allow the mind to wander;

rather, each element should be visualized individually. Every leaf, every jewel, every ray of light, every pedestal, and every banner must be made distinct and clear, as if seeing the reflection of one's own face in a mirror.
When this visualization is perfected, one eradicates the sins of birth and death accumulated over five hundred billion kalpas and will certainly be reborn in the World of Ultimate Bliss.
One who performs this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation.
"If one perceives it otherwise, it is called false perception.
The Buddha told Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"Having seen these things, you should next visualize the Buddha."
Why is this so? Because the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are the body of the Dharma-realm, pervading and entering into the thoughts and minds of all sentient beings.
Therefore, when you contemplate the Buddha in your minds, that very mind is itself the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary characteristics.
This mind creates the Buddha; this mind is the Buddha.

The ocean of the Buddhas' right and universal knowledge arises from the thoughts of the mind; therefore, you should single-mindedly fix your mindfulness and contemplate that Buddha—the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—with clear observation.
Regarding the visualization of that Buddha, one should first form a mental image.
Whether with eyes closed or open, one sees a precious image, the color of Jāmbūnada gold, seated upon that flower.

Once the image had been seated, his mind’s eye opened; he saw with perfect clarity the Land of Ultimate Bliss adorned with the seven treasures, with jeweled grounds, jeweled ponds, and rows of jeweled trees, while celestial jeweled canopies covered the treetops and nets of various jewels filled the void of space.
Seeing these matters, one should make them extremely clear, as if observing them in the palm of one's hand.
Having seen this, one should further create a great lotus flower on the left side of the Buddha, identical in every respect to the previous lotus flower.

Furthermore, visualize another great lotus flower to the right of the Buddha, and imagine an image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva seated upon the left lotus seat, likewise emitting golden light no different from before.
Visualize an image of the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta seated upon a flower-seat to the right.
When this visualization is accomplished, the images of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas all emit wondrous light;
that light is golden in color and illuminates the various jewel-trees.
Beneath each tree there are likewise three lotus flowers, and upon each lotus flower is the image of one Buddha and two Bodhisattvas, filling that land entirely.

When this visualization is accomplished, the practitioner shall hear the flowing water, the radiance, the various jewel trees, and the wild ducks, geese, and mandarin ducks all preaching the sublime Dharma.
Whether emerging from or entering meditative absorption, one constantly hears the sublime Dharma.
Whatever the practitioner hears, they should maintain it in mind without letting it go upon emerging from concentration, ensuring that it accords with the Sūtras.
If one does not correspond [to reality], it is called false conceptualization (*vikalpa*); if one corresponds with it, it is called coarse perception of the World of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
This is "visualizing perception," and it is named the Eighth Meditation.

One who practices this contemplation eliminates the offenses of birth and death accumulated over immeasurable billions of kalpas and attains the Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha within their present body.
One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation.
"If one contemplates otherwise, it is called false contemplation.
The Buddha told Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"Once this visualization is accomplished, you should next further contemplate the physical marks and radiant light of Amitāyus Buddha."
Ānanda, you should know that the body of Amitāyus Buddha is like the color of Jambūnada gold from the Yāma Heaven, multiplied by hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis.
The height of the Buddha’s body is sixty million billion nayutas of *gaṅgā*-sands of *yojanas*.
The white tuft of hair between his eyebrows curls to the right in elegant spirals, like five Mount Sumerus;
the Buddha’s eyes are as pure as the waters of the four great oceans, crystal clear and distinct.
From all the pores of his body, he emitted radiance like Mount Sumeru;
the halo of that Buddha was as vast as ten billion trichiliocosms,
and within that halo were manifested Buddhas as numerous as the sands of ten million billion nayutas of Ganges Rivers.
Each of these transformation Buddhas is likewise attended by a multitude of countless transformation Bodhisattvas.
Amitāyus Buddha possesses eighty-four thousand primary marks;
within each mark, there are eighty-four thousand secondary signs of physical excellence.
Within each and every mark of excellence, there are further eighty-four thousand rays of light;
each ray of light shines universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions, embracing and never forsaking those sentient beings who mindfully recite the Buddha's name.
Their radiant marks and signs, as well as the manifested Buddhas, cannot be fully described;
one should simply bring them to mind through recollection so that the heart sees them clearly.
One who sees these things sees all the Buddhas of the ten directions; because one sees all the Buddhas, it is called the Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha.
One who practices this contemplation is said to contemplate the bodies of all Buddhas; by contemplating the Buddha-body, one also perceives the Buddha-mind.
The mind of all Buddhas is great compassion, which gathers in all sentient beings through unconditioned compassion (*nirālamba-karuṇā*).
Those who practice this visualization will, upon leaving their bodies at the end of this life, be born before all Buddhas and attain the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Therefore, the wise should fix their minds and contemplate Amitāyus Buddha with earnest attention.
Regarding the visualization of Amitāyus Buddha, one enters through a single mark and excellence; simply visualize the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows until it is perfectly clear.
Once the mark of the white tuft of hair between the eyebrows is seen, the eighty-four thousand marks and excellences will naturally be perceived.
One who beholds Amitāyus Buddha beholds the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions;
because they behold these infinite Buddhas, they receive their prediction of enlightenment in the presence of those Buddhas.
This is the universal contemplation of all perceptions of form; it is called the ninth contemplation.
One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation.
If one contemplates otherwise, it is called wrong contemplation.
The Buddha told Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"Once you have clearly and distinctly beheld Amitāyus Buddha, you should next contemplate Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva."

This Bodhisattva’s body is eighty billion nayuta Ganges-sands of yojanas in height; his body is the color of purple-gold, he has a fleshly protuberance upon his head, a halo surrounds his neck, and each of his faces spans hundreds of thousands of yojanas.
Within his halo were five hundred transformation Buddhas, each identical to Śākyamuni.
Each of these transformation Buddhas had five hundred bodhisattvas and immeasurable devas serving as their attendants.
Within the light emanating from his entire body, the forms and appearances of all sentient beings of the five realms of existence are clearly manifested.
Upon his head is a celestial crown fashioned from the exquisite *vaidūrya* (lapis lazuli) *maṇi* jewel.
Within his celestial crown stands an emanation Buddha twenty-five yojanas in height.
The face of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is the color of Jāmbūnada gold;
the tuft of hair between his eyebrows possesses the colors of the seven jewels and radiates eighty-four thousand varieties of light.
Each ray of light contains immeasurable and countless hundreds of thousands of manifested Buddhas;
each manifested Buddha has countless manifested Bodhisattvas as attendants, manifesting with sovereign mastery throughout the realms of the ten directions.
His arms were the color of red lotuses, adorned with eighty billion subtle and wondrous rays of light as necklaces;
within those necklaces, all manner of adornments were universally manifested.
The palms are the color of five hundred billion variegated lotuses;
on each of the ten fingertips, there are eighty-four thousand lines, like the patterns of a seal.
Each individual painting contains eighty-four thousand colors;
each color emits eighty-four thousand rays of light. These rays are soft and supple, universally illuminating all things, and with these jewel-hands, he receives and guides sentient beings.
When he lifts his foot, beneath his feet there appear the marks of thousand-spoked wheels, which spontaneously transform into five hundred billion towers of light.
When he sets his foot down, there are diamond-maṇi flowers that scatter everywhere until they completely fill all space.

His remaining physical characteristics were fully endowed with all the marks of excellence, no different from those of a Buddha; however, only his cranial protuberance (*uṣṇīṣa*) and the mark of the invisible crown of the head (*anavalokitamūrdhatā*) did not equal those of the World-Honored One.
"This is the contemplation of the true physical marks of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara; it is called the tenth contemplation.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"If you wish to contemplate the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, you should perform this contemplation."
Those who practice this contemplation will not encounter any calamities; they will purify their karmic obstructions and eliminate the sins of birth and death accumulated over incalculable eons.
For such a Bodhisattva, merely hearing his name brings immeasurable merit—how much more so for those who contemplate him with true insight!
If there are those who wish to contemplate the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, they should first contemplate the *uṣṇīṣa* on his crown, and next contemplate his celestial crown.
They should then contemplate the remaining marks in successive order until all are clearly perceived, as if looking at the palm of one's hand.
"One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation;
one who contemplates otherwise is said to practice wrong contemplation.
The Buddha then addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"Next, one contemplates the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta.

The physical dimensions of this Bodhisattva are also like those of Avalokiteśvara; his halo measures two hundred and twenty-five *yojanas* across its face and illuminates an area of two hundred and fifty *yojanas*."
The radiance from his entire body illuminates the lands of the ten directions, manifesting as a purple-gold color.
All sentient beings with whom he has a karmic connection are able to see it.

Upon seeing the light from even a single pore of this Bodhisattva, they immediately behold the pure and wondrous radiance of the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions; for this reason, this Bodhisattva is named Boundless Light (Anantaprabha).
With the light of wisdom, he universally illumines all beings, causing them to leave the three miserable realms and attain supreme power; for this reason, this bodhisattva is named Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
This Bodhisattva’s celestial crown has five hundred precious lotus flowers;
each precious flower has five hundred precious pedestals.
Within each pedestal, the vast and expansive characteristics of the pure and wondrous lands of the Buddhas of the ten directions all appear.
His uṣṇīṣa on the crown of his head is like a padma flower.
Upon this uṣṇīṣa is a precious vase filled with various radiances that universally manifest the deeds of a Buddha.
His other physical marks are identical to those of Avalokiteśvara, without any difference whatsoever.
When this Bodhisattva walks, all the worlds of the ten directions tremble; wherever the earth shakes, there appear five hundred billion precious flowers.
Each precious flower is magnificently adorned and exalted, like the world of Ultimate Bliss.
When this Bodhisattva sits, the lands of the seven jewels tremble all at once.

From the Buddha-field of Golden Light below to the Buddha-field of King of Radiance above, all the emanations of Amitāyus Buddha—as numerous as the atoms of immeasurable worlds—along with the emanations of Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, gather like clouds in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Filling the air, they sit upon lotus thrones and expound the wondrous Dharma, delivering sentient beings from suffering.
One who performs this contemplation is said to be "contemplating and seeing the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta";
this constitutes the contemplation of the physical marks of Mahāsthāmaprāpta’s body.
This contemplation of the Bodhisattva is called the eleventh contemplation; it eliminates the sins of birth and death accumulated over incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.
Those who practice this contemplation will not dwell within a womb, but shall constantly roam through the pure and wondrous lands of all Buddhas.
Once this contemplation is perfected, they are said to be fully endowed with the contemplations of Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
"One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation;
if one contemplates otherwise, it is called wrong contemplation.
The Buddha then addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī:

"When seeing this phenomenon, one should give rise to the perception and mental resolve that one sees oneself born in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, sitting cross-legged within a lotus flower; one should form the perception of the lotus closing and the perception of the lotus opening."
When the lotus blossoms, one should imagine five hundred colored rays of light coming to illuminate the body;

when the eyes open, one sees Buddhas and Bodhisattvas filling the void of space. The sounds produced by the water birds, the forest trees, and the various Buddhas all expound the wondrous Dharma, in harmony with the twelve divisions of the scriptures.
If, upon emerging from meditative absorption, one maintains this recollection without loss and beholds these things,
it is called "beholding the Buddha Amitāyus and the World of Ultimate Bliss.
This is the visualization of Universal Contemplation, known as the Twelfth Meditation.
The Buddha of Immeasurable Life manifests countless transformation bodies, which, together with Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, constantly come to the place where this practitioner dwells.
One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation.
"If one contemplates otherwise, it is called false contemplation.
The Buddha told Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"If you wish to give rise to a sincere heart for the Western Quarter, you should first contemplate the image of one zhang and six chi standing upon the waters of the pond."
As previously stated, the physical dimensions of Amitāyus Buddha are boundless and are beyond the reach of the mental power of ordinary beings.
Nevertheless, by virtue of that Tathāgata’s power of past vows, those who bring him to mind with recollection and contemplation will certainly attain accomplishment.
If merely contemplating the image of the Buddha yields immeasurable merit, how much more so when one contemplates the Buddha’s fully perfected physical marks!
Amitābha Buddha possesses supernormal powers at will, manifesting himself with sovereign mastery throughout the lands of the ten directions.
Sometimes he manifests a great body that fills the void of space;
sometimes he manifests a small body of sixteen or eight feet.
All manifested forms are of a true golden color, with circular halos, emanated Buddhas, and precious lotus flowers, as described above.

The Bodhisattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta manifest bodies identical to those of sentient beings in all places; yet, by observing their heads alone, one knows this is Avalokiteśvara and that is Mahāsthāmaprāpta. These two bodhisattvas assist Amitābha Buddha in universally transforming all beings.
This is the contemplation of mixed perceptions; it is called the thirteenth contemplation.
One who performs this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation.
If one contemplates otherwise, it is called false contemplation.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī:
"In general, there are nine grades of persons born in the Western Land.
Regarding those of the highest grade in the highest birth: if there are sentient beings who wish to be born in that land and give rise to three kinds of mind, they shall immediately attain rebirth."
What are these three?
First, the sincere mind;
second, the profound mind.
Third is the mind of dedication and aspiration.
One who possesses these three minds will certainly be born in that land.
Furthermore, there are three kinds of sentient beings who shall attain rebirth there.
What are these three?
First, to refrain from killing with a mind of loving-kindness and to fulfill all precepts and practices.
Second, to read and recite the Mahāyāna Vaipulya sūtras.
Third, one should practice the six recollections and dedicate the merit toward the aspiration to be born in that Buddha-land.
Possessing these merits, after one day up to seven days, one will immediately attain rebirth there.

When one is born in that land, because this person has practiced with such diligence and vigor, Amitābha Tathāgata, along with Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, countless transformation Buddhas, hundreds of thousands of bhikṣus, the great assembly of śrāvakas, immeasurable devas, and palaces of the seven jewels, will appear before the practitioner. Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, holding a vajra platform, together with Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, will arrive before the practitioner.
Amitābha Buddha emits great radiance that illuminates the practitioner’s body, extending his hands to welcome them.
Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and countless bodhisattvas praise the practitioner and encourage their resolve.
Having seen this, the practitioner leaps for joy.
Seeing himself mounted upon a vajra pedestal, following behind the Buddha, he is reborn in that land in the time it takes to snap one's fingers.
Having been born in that land, one beholds the physical body of the Buddha, complete with all its marks; one beholds the bodhisattvas, complete with their physical marks;
and sees the jewel groves of radiant light expounding the sublime Dharma.
Upon hearing this, they immediately realized the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
In a mere moment, they served various Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions, receiving successive predictions of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*) before each of those Buddhas.
Upon returning to their native lands, they attain immeasurable hundreds of thousands of *dhāraṇī* gates; these are called those of the highest grade of the highest birth.
"As for those of the highest grade of middle birth, it is not necessary that they uphold, read, or recite the Vaipulya sūtras."
Skillfully understanding the meaning and intent, their minds are not startled or shaken by the ultimate truth; they have deep faith in cause and effect and do not slander the Mahāyāna;
by means of these merits, they dedicate them toward the vow to seek rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

When the life of one who practices this path is about to end, Amitābha Buddha, together with Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, surrounded by an immeasurable multitude of followers and retinues, will arrive before the practitioner holding a purple-golden platform and say in praise:
"O Son of the Dharma!..."
"You practice the Mahāyāna and understand the ultimate truth; therefore, I have now come to welcome you.
Simultaneously, a thousand manifested Buddhas extended their hands.

The practitioner saw himself seated upon a purple-golden pedestal, joining his palms and reverently praising the Buddhas. In the space of a single thought-moment, he was reborn within the seven-jeweled pond of that land.
This purple-golden terrace is like a great precious flower, which opens immediately after one night has passed.
The practitioner’s body becomes the color of purple-polished gold, and beneath his feet there are also lotus flowers made of the seven treasures.
The Buddha and the bodhisattvas together emit radiance that illuminates the practitioner’s body, and their eyes immediately open with clarity.
Due to their prior habitual practice, they universally hear various sounds, all of which exclusively expound the profound ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*).
He immediately descended from the golden platform, prostrated before the Buddha with palms joined, and praised the World-Honored One.
After seven days had passed, he attained non-retrogression regarding Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi at that very moment.
At that very moment, they are able to fly to the ten directions to serve various Buddhas in succession, cultivating various samādhis in the presence of those Buddhas.

After the passing of one small kalpa, they attain the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti) and receive a prediction of enlightenment before their eyes; these are called those of superior grade who are born from middle [roots].

"As for those of the highest grade who are born in the lower level, they likewise believe in cause and effect and do not slander the Mahāyāna; they merely resolve their minds upon the unsurpassed path and, by means of these merits, dedicate them toward the vow to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss."

When that practitioner’s life is about to end, Amitābha Buddha, along with Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, together with their retinues, holding golden lotus flowers and manifesting five hundred transformation Buddhas, come to welcome this person.
Five hundred manifested Buddhas simultaneously extended their hands and praised him, saying:
"O Son of the Dharma!
You are now pure; having resolved upon the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment, we have come to welcome you."
Upon seeing this, one immediately sees oneself sitting upon a golden lotus flower.
Once seated, the flower closes; following behind the World-Honored One, one then attains rebirth within a pond of the seven treasures.
After one day and one night, the lotus flower finally opened; within seven days, he was able to see the Buddha.
Although he saw the Buddha’s body, his mind was not clear regarding the excellence of its various marks; it was only after three weeks that he saw them with perfect clarity.
Hearing all manner of sounds, they all expound the wondrous Dharma.
Traveling throughout the ten directions, they make offerings to all Buddhas.
Before these Buddhas, they hear the most profound teachings; after three minor kalpas, they attain the Gate of Illumination of the Hundred Dharmas and dwell on the Stage of Joy.
This is called "those who are born in the lower grade of the highest class.
This is termed the perception of birth in the highest class, and it is called the fourteenth contemplation.
One who performs this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation.
"If one views it otherwise, it is called a false view.
The Buddha told Ānanda and Vaidehī: "Regarding those of the highest grade in the middle level of rebirth:

if there are sentient beings who receive and uphold the five precepts, observe the eightfold fast, practice various moral disciplines, do not commit the five heinous crimes, and are free from all faults and evils;"
By means of these roots of goodness, one dedicates them with the vow to seek rebirth in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.

When the practitioner approaches the end of life, Amitābha Buddha, surrounded by a retinue of bhikṣus and followers, will emit golden light that reaches the person and proclaim suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self, praising the renunciation of the household life as the means to escape all sufferings.
Having seen this, the practitioner’s heart was filled with great joy.
He saw himself sitting upon a lotus pedestal, kneeling upright with palms joined in prostration before the Buddha.
Before his head had even been raised, he attained rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and the lotus flower immediately opened.

When the flowers bloom, they hear various sounds praising the Four Noble Truths; at that moment, they immediately attain the path of Arhatship, possessing the three types of supernormal knowledge (*traividyā*), the six supernatural powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), and the eight liberations (*aṣṭavimokṣa*).
These are called those who are born in the middle grade of the superior class.

"Regarding those born in the middle grade of the intermediate state: if there are sentient beings who, for one day and one night, observe the eight precepts and the fast; or for one day and one night, observe the śrāmaṇera precepts; or for one day and one night, observe the full precepts (upasaṃpadā), with their dignified deportment (īryāpatha) remaining flawless."
By this merit, one should dedicate it with the vow to seek rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Perfumed by the fragrance of the precepts, when such a practitioner is about to pass away, they will see Amitābha Buddha together with his retinue emitting golden light and holding a seven-jeweled lotus flower before them. The practitioner will personally hear a voice from the air praising them, saying:
"O son of good family!..."
"Because you, a virtuous person, have followed the teachings of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, I have come to welcome you.
The practitioner sees himself seated upon a lotus flower; the lotus flower then closes, and he is reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Within the jewel pond, the lotus blossomed after seven days had passed.
Once the flower had opened, he opened his eyes, joined his palms, and praised the World-Honored One.
Hearing the Dharma, he rejoiced and attained the stage of Srotāpanna; after half an eon, he became an Arhat.
This is called "being born among those of middle capacity in the middle grade.

As for "those of middle capacity in the lower grade": if there are good men or good women who filially support their parents and practice worldly benevolence and righteousness, when this person’s life is about to end, they encounter a virtuous friend who extensively explains to them the joyful matters of Amitābha Buddha’s land and also expounds upon the forty-eight great vows of the Bhikṣu Dharmākara.
Having heard this matter, he immediately passed away.
In the time it takes a strong man to bend and extend his arm, he was reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
Seven days after his birth there, he encountered Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta; hearing the Dharma with joy, he attained the stage of Srotāpanna.
After the passing of one small kalpa, he attains arhatship.
This is called the one who is born in the lower grade of the middle class.
This is termed the perception of birth in the middle grade, and it is named the Fifteenth Contemplation.
"One who practices this contemplation is said to practice right contemplation;
one who contemplates otherwise is said to practice wrong contemplation.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī:

"Regarding those who are reborn in the lower grade of the superior level: there may be sentient beings who have committed various evil deeds; although they do not slander the Vaipulya sutras, such foolish people have produced many unwholesome dharmas and lack a sense of shame or remorse. When their lives are about to end, they encounter a virtuous friend who praises for them the titles and names of the twelve divisions of the Mahayana sutras."
By hearing the names of these various sutras, one eliminates the most grievous evil karma accumulated over a thousand kalpas.
Furthermore, the wise teacher instructs them to join their palms and, with hands clasped, recite "Namo Amitābha Buddha."
"By virtue of reciting the Buddha's name, the sins of birth and death accumulated over fifty billion kalpas shall be eliminated.

At that time, that Buddha will immediately dispatch emanated Buddhas, an emanated Avalokiteśvara, and an emanated Mahāsthāmaprāpta to appear before the practitioner and praise them, saying: 'Excellent!'"
"O son of good family!
Because you have invoked the name of the Buddha, all your sins are extinguished; I come to welcome you.
Having spoken these words, the practitioner immediately beholds the light of the transformation Buddha filling his room. Upon seeing this, he rejoices and then passes away.
Riding upon a precious lotus flower and following behind the transformation Buddha, they are born within a pool of jewels; after seven times seven days have passed, the lotus flower finally unfolds.

At the moment the flower blooms, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of Great Compassion and the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta emit great radiance and stand before that person, preaching the profound twelvefold division of the scriptures for them.
Having heard this, they believe and understand it, and resolve their minds upon the unsurpassed path.
After ten minor kalpas, they become fully endowed with the gate of illumination of the hundred dharmas and attain entry into the first stage;
these are called those who are born in the highest grade of the lower level.
“Upon hearing the name of the Buddha, the name of the Dharma, and the name of the Sangha—by hearing the names of the Triple Gem, one immediately attains rebirth there.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī:

“As for those of the middle birth in the lowest grade: there may be sentient beings who violate the five precepts, the eight precepts, or the full set of precepts. Such foolish people steal the property of the Sangha, pilfer the goods belonging to the present community of monks, preach the Dharma with impurity, and lack any sense of shame or remorse, adorning themselves with various evil dharmas.”
Such a sinner, on account of their evil karma, ought to fall into hell.

As their life is about to end, the various fires of hell arrive all at once; yet, encountering a spiritual friend who possesses great compassion, they are immediately praised and taught of the ten powers and majestic virtue of Amitābha Buddha. This friend extensively praises that Buddha’s radiance and supernatural power, and likewise praises his morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.
Upon hearing this, that person shall have the karmic offenses of birth and death from eighty billion kalpas eradicated.
The fierce fires of hell will transform into cool breezes, blowing celestial flowers.
Upon each flower there will be an emanated Buddha and Bodhisattva to welcome this person.
In the space of a single thought-moment, one immediately attains rebirth within a lotus flower inside a pond of the seven treasures; after six kalpas have passed, the lotus flower finally opens.
At the moment the flower blooms, Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta comfort that person with Brahma-sounds and preach for them the profound Mahāyāna sūtras.
Having heard this Dharma, they immediately gave rise to the aspiration for supreme enlightenment at that very moment.
This is called "one born in the middle grade of the lower level.
The Buddha addressed Ānanda and Vaidehī:

Regarding those born in the lowest grade of the lowest level: there may be sentient beings who commit unwholesome deeds, such as the five heinous crimes and the ten evil acts, fully possessing all manner of unwholesomeness.
Because of these evil karmas, such deluded persons ought to fall into the evil realms and undergo suffering without end for many kalpas.

When such a foolish person approaches the end of life, they may encounter a virtuous friend who offers various forms of consolation, preaches the sublime Dharma for them, and instructs them to practice mindfulness of the Buddha; yet, being oppressed by suffering, that person has no leisure to practice mindfulness of the Buddha.
The virtuous friend said:
"If you are unable to bring that Buddha to mind, you should instead recite the invocation: 'Homage to Amitāyus Buddha.
In this way, with a sincere heart, maintain an uninterrupted voice and complete ten recitations, calling out: 'Namo Amitābha Buddha.'"
By virtue of reciting the Buddha’s name, in every thought-moment, one eliminates the sins of birth and death accumulated over eight billion kalpas.

At the time of death, one will see a golden lotus flower, like a sun-disk, appearing before that person; in the space of a single thought-moment, one shall attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Within the lotus flower, twelve great kalpas will pass before it finally opens.

When the flower blooms, Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, with voices of great compassion, shall extensively expound the true nature (*tathatā*) for that person and teach the methods for extinguishing their transgressions.
Having heard this, they rejoice and immediately give rise to the bodhicitta at that very moment;
these are called those who are born in the lowest grade of the lower level.
This is termed the perception of birth in the lower grade, and it is called the sixteenth visualization.

At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken these words, Vaidehī and her five hundred attendants, upon hearing what the Buddha had said, immediately beheld the vast and expansive features of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and they were able to see the body of the Buddha as well as the two Bodhisattvas.

Their hearts were filled with joy, and they marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence; they attained sudden and great enlightenment, realizing the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharmakṣānti*).
Five hundred female attendants resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and vowed to be reborn in that land.
The World-Honored One bestowed predictions upon them all, declaring that they would all be reborn there; having been born in that land, they would attain the Samādhi of the Presence of All Buddhas.
Immeasurable devas also resolved their minds upon the Unsurpassed Way.
At that time, Ānanda rose from his seat, approached the Buddha, and said to him:
“World-Honored One,
what should this sutra be named?”
"What is the essential method for receiving and upholding this Dharma?
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"This sutra is titled 'The Visualization of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, Amitāyus Buddha, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, and Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva'; it is also titled 'Purifying Karmic Obstructions and Being Born Before All Buddhas.'"
"You should receive and uphold this, lest you forget or lose it!
Those who practice this samādhi shall, in their present bodies, behold Amitāyus Buddha and the two Great Beings.

If good sons or good daughters merely hear the name of the Buddha and the names of the two Bodhisattvas, they will eliminate the sins of birth and death accumulated over immeasurable kalpas; how much more so if they bring them to mind!"

If there are those who practice mindfulness of the Buddha, you should know that such persons are like *puṇḍarīka* flowers among humanity; Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva will be their supreme friends, and they shall sit at the site of enlightenment and be born into the family of all Buddhas.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"You should well uphold these words.
To uphold these words is to uphold the name of Amitāyus Buddha."
When the Buddha had spoken these words, the Venerable Maudgalyāyana, the Venerable Ānanda, Vaidehī, and the others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly filled with joy.
At that time, the World-Honored One ascended into the void with his feet and returned to Vulture Peak Mountain.
Then, Ānanda extensively recounted the aforementioned events for the great assembly.
Immeasurable humans, devas, nāgas, spirits, and yakṣas, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they paid homage to the Buddha and withdrew.
Thus ends the *Sūtra on the Visualization of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life*.
